title: kv-residency-scanner-and-pressure-aware-defragger: reduce fragmentation and spill bursts under mixed workloads
author: Aisha Kapoor
description: Motivation: In production mixed workloads we observed recurring short-lived spill bursts and sustained KV cache fragmentation that increased tail latency and token cost. This PR introduces a residency scanner that maintains per-segment hotness and a pressure-aware defragger which uses a weighted eviction score and opportunistic micro-compaction to reduce fragmentation without impacting latency SLOs. Summary of changes: 1) residency scanner: background thread that periodically samples segment residency and maintains a compacted LRU-like heatmap; 2) pressure-aware defragger: when free-slot fragmentation exceeds thresholds, scheduler launches short micro-compactions on low-hotness segments and redistributes large cold ranges to contiguous pages; 3) weighted evictor: eviction score now includes residency age, fragmentation penalty, and request-cost weight (queried from router telemetry) so evictions favor low-impact keys; 4) spill smoothing: added spill burst detector that throttles async spill workers and coalesces small spill tasks into page-aligned batches; 5) continuous-batching interaction: scheduler now pins frequently accessed KV pages across micro-batch windows to avoid thrash; 6) tracing/metrics: added kv.residency.* and kv.defrag.* metrics and tracing hooks for canary rollouts. Testing & validation: unit tests for scanner/defragger logic, integration test that simulates mixed chat+embedding workload and asserts <5% increase in p99 latency and 18-30% reduction in spill IOPS at sustained high load, chaos test with forced OOM to validate graceful spill fallback. Rollout plan: feature gated behind kv_defrag_v2 flag, canary in Dedicated region eu-west-1 on 3 tenants with telemetry review, gradual ramp to all hosts over 72 hours. Related: builds on ENG-1840 (adaptive-evictor) and fixes SUP-7241 incident reproduction where short-lived hotkeys caused repeated small spills. Breaking changes: none.
commits: Add residency scanner core and unit tests
Implement pressure-aware defragger and micro-compaction kernel selection
Weighted evictor: eviction scoring and telemetry hooks
Spill smoothing: coalescer and throttler for async spill workers
Add metrics, tracing, and feature gate
Fix: reclamation race in high-concurrency path (sync -> atomic handoff)
Docs: runbook entry for kv_defrag_v2 rollout and troubleshooting
review_comments: Diego Martin: The residency sampling rate looks conservative for 48-core hosts; can we make it adaptive to CPU pressure?
Aisha Kapoor: Good catch — added adaptive rate control that backs off sampling when per-host CPU > 70% (see defrag_scheduler.cpp).
Sofia Chen: Need a guard to ensure micro-compaction doesn't hold page locks across RPC boundaries; add timeout to compaction op.
Aisha Kapoor: Added op-level timeouts and lock-tier escalation to prevent long-held locks; also added a Prometheus alert kv.defrag.lock_holds > 5s.
Ravi Patel: CI flaked on a race in the reclaim path under ASan — I repro'd and suggested an atomic handoff; tests pass now.
QA: Verified metric names, added integration test scenarios with embedding-heavy workload, canary telemetry looks good.
Security: Reviewed no new surface for secrets; feature flag gating accepted.
PM (Ana Lopez): Confirmed rollout windows and stakeholders for Dedicated tenants; approved for gradual rollout.
ci_checks: benchmarks: baseline against main: 95th p99 latency within SLO
release_notes: Introduce KV residency scanner and pressure-aware defragger to reduce KV cache fragmentation and smooth spill bursts; improves sustained spill IOPS by ~20-30% in mixed workloads and reduces eviction-induced latency spikes. Feature gated behind kv_defrag_v2.
